extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent agents (including registered foreign practitioners), and other authorized representatives interacting with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing who may act for applicants/patentees, default correspondence, disregarded communications, ownership/transfer recording, and correcting applicant/inventor names or identities in Canadian patent applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of authorization requirement (limited circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not generally require proof of authorization for persons said to be authorized by applicants/patentees, but does require proof when a registered foreign practitioner is signing the appointment of a patent agent, signing a small entity declaration, or requesting an interview with a patent examiner (subsections 27, 44 and 39 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a registered foreign practitioner is acting in these specified capacities, an authorizing document signed by the applicant/common representative/patentee (as applicable) must be submitted. In other cases the Office will implicitly assume authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointed agent or associate may act for specified actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Manual refers to 'the appointed patent agent', the specified action may be taken by the appointed patent agent or by the appointed associate patent agent if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all agents at a firm are appointed (or appointed as associate), any individual agent at that firm may take the specified action (i.e., firm-level appointment confers authority to individual agents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing applications and paying application/national phase fees — who may act
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an application, paying the application fee, or submitting the request to enter the PCT national phase and paying associated fees may be done by the appointed patent agent, the applicant (any applicant if joint applicants), or any person authorized by any of the applicants (subsection 36(2) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These permissions apply at the application stage; see related sections for differences post-grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of annual maintenance fees (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees for applications (and corresponding late fees) may be paid by the appointed patent agent, the applicant (any applicant if there are joint applicants), or any person authorized by any of the applicants (subsection 36(2) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: for maintenance payments after grant, see the patents-specific section (5.07.03a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of other application-related fees
rubrics_metrics.description: All other fees related to a patent application, such as the final fee, may be paid by the appointed patent agent, the single applicant, or the common representative (subsection 36(5) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there are joint applicants, payment of certain fees is more restricted (e.g., a non-agent person may not be acceptable unless specifically authorized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing a small entity declaration (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity declaration may be signed by the appointed patent agent, the applicant (any applicant if joint), or a registered foreign practitioner authorized by the applicant if a proof of authorization signed by the applicant is submitted (paragraph 44(3)(c) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of authorization must be provided when a registered foreign practitioner signs; see cross-reference to section 5.07.03d for post-grant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after abandonment for failure to pay maintenance fee (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application has been deemed abandoned for failure to pay a maintenance fee, the necessary steps to reinstate the application may be taken by the appointed patent agent, the single applicant, or the common representative (subsection 36(5) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinstatement pathway is for abandonment due to maintenance non-payment; reinstatement for other reasons may have different permissive actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting request to record a transfer (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may submit a request to record a transfer under subsection 49(2) of the Patent Act depends on whether there is a single applicant or joint applicants and on which applicants’ rights are being transferred; permitted submitters include the appointed patent agent, the applicant, any person authorized by the applicant, the common representative, a person authorized by the common representative, the joint applicant whose rights are being transferred, and any person authorized by that joint applicant (subsection 36(3) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the transferee submits the request, the transferee may represent themselves or be represented by any person authorized by them. Carefully check which combination of permissions applies to the particular transfer scenario (single vs joint; single-joint rights vs multiple).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to record a name change (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a single applicant, a request to record a name change may be submitted by the appointed patent agent, the applicant, or any person authorized by the applicant; if joint applicants, by the appointed patent agent, the common representative, or any person authorized by the common representative (subsection 36(4) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different actors are authorized depending on single vs joint applicant status; ensure appropriate authorization is documented where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting references to prior applications or additions to specification/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to a previously filed application (section 27.01 Patent Act) or an addition to the specification or additional drawing (section 28.01 Patent Act) may be submitted by the appointed patent agent or by the single applicant or common representative (subsection 36(5) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These submissions are more restricted than certain fee payments; check whether an appointed agent exists and whether the common representative must act for joint applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview with patent examiner — who may conduct (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent agent has been appointed, interviews may be conducted by the appointed patent agent; by the single applicant with permission of the appointed patent agent; by a registered foreign practitioner authorized by the single applicant with permission of the appointed patent agent (with an authorizing document signed by the single applicant); by the common representative with permission of the appointed patent agent; or by a registered foreign practitioner authorized by the common representative with permission and signed authorizing document. If no patent agent has been appointed and is not required, the single applicant or the common representative may have the interview (section 39 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews require the appointed agent’s permission when an agent is appointed; registered foreign practitioners additionally require written authorization by the applicant/common representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of applicant identity — who must request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requested correction is being made under section 104 or subsection 154(6) of the Patent Rules, the person who submitted the application or paid the basic national fee required to enter the PCT national phase must request correction of the applicant’s identity. Other types of corrections to the name or identity must be made by the appointed patent agent (if appointed) or, if no agent, by the single applicant or common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different correction pathways exist depending on type of correction (identity vs name) and whether an agent is appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation summary principles (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables summarize who can act for various actions depending on whether a patent agent is appointed or not, and depending on single applicant, common representative, registered foreign practitioner, or any person authorized by applicant(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the tables for a matrix of permitted actors per action; exceptions (e.g., small entity signing, payment of other fees) are indicated in the tables and footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant representation — who may act for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a patent is granted, a single patentee may represent themselves or be represented by any person authorized by them; joint patentees may be represented by the common representative or by any person authorized by the common representative (subsection 37(1) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents, an authorized person may include but is not limited to an appointed patent agent or associate agent. Some exceptions require proof of authorization (e.g., registered foreign practitioner signing appointment or small entity declaration — sections 28 and 112 Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of annual maintenance fees (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees for patents (and corresponding late fees) may be paid by the appointed patent agent, the patentee (any patentee if joint patentees), or any person authorized by any of the patentees (subsection 37(1) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining payment rights post-grant mirrors application-stage rules but uses patentee terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting request to record a transfer (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents, who may submit a request to record a transfer under subsection 49(3) of the Patent Act depends on single vs joint patentees; permitted actors include the appointed patent agent, the patentee, any person authorized by the patentee, the common representative, a person authorized by the common representative, the joint patentee whose rights are being transferred, and any person authorized by that joint patentee (paragraph 37(1)(a) and subparagraph 37(1)(b)(ii) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the transferee requests recording, they may represent themselves or be represented by any person authorized by them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional term, reissue, disclaimer, re-examination — who may act (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: For making observations, applying for additional term, reissuance, disclaimers, filing a reply, or participating in re-examination: if single patentee, the single patentee or an appointed patent agent; if joint patentees, the common representative or an appointed patent agent (subsection 37(2) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These post-grant substantive proceedings are more restricted: joint actions normally require common representative or agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing a small entity declaration (patents and re-examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity declaration for a patent may be signed by the appointed patent agent, the patentee (any patentee if joint), or a registered foreign practitioner authorized by the patentee if a proof of authorization signed by the patentee is submitted (paragraph 112(3)(c) Patent Rules). For re-examination, a small entity declaration may be signed by the patent agent appointed by the person requesting re-examination, the person requesting re-examination, or a registered foreign practitioner authorized by that person with proof signed by the requester (paragraph 122(4)(d) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required authorization documents accompany filings when a registered foreign practitioner signs; cross-reference application-stage rules for differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default correspondent for Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will send all correspondence regarding a patent application or patent to the appointed patent agent (or appointed associate by default if one is appointed). If all agents at a firm are appointed, correspondence will be sent to the firm. If no patent agent is appointed, the Office will send correspondence to the common representative (for joint applicants/patentees) or the single applicant/patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include notices of disregarded communication, agent revocation notifications, responses to requests to record a transfer, responses to requests for examination, and correspondence with third parties submitting prior art, protests, or re-examination requests (see section 5.08 for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disregarded communications — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will have regard to written communications only from persons authorized to represent applicants and patentees as outlined in sections 33 to 37 of the Patent Rules. Written communications from others will be disregarded, except in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a communication is disregarded, the Office will send a notice of disregarded communication and give the sender an opportunity to comply with the Patent Rules and have the Office give regard to the original communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions that avoid immediate disregarded communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Three exceptions where a communication appearing unauthorized will trigger a notice (rather than immediate acceptance): (1) an applicant/patentee who is not the common representative communicates to take an action that may be taken by the common representative; (2) a patent agent who is not appointed communicates with the Office; (3) a communication appears to come from a patent agent but the name of the sender is not provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these three circumstances a notice of disregarded communication is sent and the person is given three months (in most cases) to rectify (e.g., appointment or provision of name) so the original communication may be considered as having been received on its original date if resolved within the timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice procedure — joint applicant/patentee not common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office receives a communication from a joint applicant or joint patentee who is not the common representative for a purpose that only the common representative may carry out, the Office must send a notice of disregarded communication to that joint applicant/patentee and a copy to the common representative (subsection 40(1) Patent Rules). The joint applicant/patentee has three months to be appointed as common representative and request the Commissioner to have regard to the initial communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appointment and request are made within the timeframe, the original communication is deemed received from the common representative on the original receipt day. These provisions do not apply to purposes that may be carried out by any joint applicant or by persons authorized by the common representative or a joint applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice procedure — patent agent not appointed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent agent communicates on behalf of an applicant/patentee but is not appointed, the Office will send a notice of disregarded communication to the patent agent indicating the communication will not be regarded unless the agent is appointed within three months and requests regard; a copy is sent to the default correspondent (subsection 41(1) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agent is subsequently appointed and requests regard within the timeframe, the original communication is deemed to have been received from the applicant/patentee on the original receipt date. This does not apply to communications for purposes that may be carried out by any person authorized by an applicant/patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice procedure — patent agent name not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a communication appears to come from a patent agent but does not provide the agent's name, the Office will send a notice requiring the person to provide their name within three months and request that the Commissioner have regard to the original communication (subsection 41.1(2) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the name is provided within the timeframe and the person was a patent agent on the date the communication was submitted, the original communication will be deemed to have been received from the patent agent on the original date. Note exceptions (e.g., certain fee payments) where the agent name is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording transfers — use of official form recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will record a transfer upon receipt of a request compliant with section 126 of the Patent Rules and payment of the prescribed fee. The Office recommends using the provided form for requests under section 126 to ensure necessary information is provided and to expedite processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording transfers updates the chain of title. Although recording is not mandatory, doing so timely has benefits (assures correct owner on record, aids public recognition of ownership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining chain of title — benefits and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording transfers/changes of owner is not mandatory but recommended to keep Patent Office records accurate, ensure patents are issued to correct owners, and make ownership easily recognizable to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed request form and pay the prescribed fee listed on CIPO’s Patent Fees webpage to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding or removing applicants (application stage) — statutory grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Under subsection 31(3) Patent Act, if joint applicants are listed and it later appears one or more had no part in the invention, the remaining applicants may continue prosecution upon satisfying the Commissioner by affidavit that they are the sole inventor(s) or legal representatives. Under subsection 31(4), a further applicant may be joined by showing they should have been joined and omission was by inadvertence/mistake and not for delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are statutory remedies for incorrect or incomplete applicant lists; appropriate affidavits or evidence of inadvertence may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Court jurisdiction over title entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 52 of the Patent Act, the Federal Court has jurisdiction on application of the Commissioner or any person interested to order that any entry in the Patent Office records relating to title to a patent be varied or expunged, including removal of a previously registered document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputes over recorded title entries can be litigated in Federal Court under this statutory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors — requirement to join application
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is made collaboratively, all inventors must join in applying for a patent; if one inventor refuses or cannot be located after diligent inquiry, the other inventors or their legal representatives may apply upon satisfying the Commissioner of refusal or inability to locate (subsection 31(1) Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully document diligence efforts to locate missing inventors or evidence of refusal to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding/removing inventors when subject-matter changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When amendments change the claimed subject-matter, inventors listed may need updating. Inventors can be added or removed under section 106(b) of the Patent Rules so long as the request is received before the day the notice of allowance or conditional notice of allowance is sent. The Office will not evaluate evidence regarding ownership in inventor disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is critical: requests after allowance may not be processed under section 106(b). If inventorship disputes involve ownership claims, separate legal proceedings may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting applicant naming errors — identity versus name
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections may be for applicant identity (wrong person named) or applicant name (spelling/nickname). The Office generally cannot determine which applies, so requesters should clearly state the type (identity or name only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedural rules and time limits apply to identity corrections versus name-only corrections; provide the appropriate statements required by the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of applicant identity — who may request and required statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who submitted the application to obtain a filing date or paid the basic national fee for PCT national phase entry may request correction of applicant identity if the error arose from inadvertence/accident/mistake without fraudulent or deceptive intention, and that person provides a statement to that effect (section 104 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit in the statement that the error was inadvertent and not fraudulent; follow timeline constraints (see 6.03.02a/b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for correcting applicant identity — regularly filed Canadian application
rubrics_metrics.description: For a regularly filed application, the request to correct applicant identity must be made before the earlier of when the application becomes open to public inspection and the day on which the Commissioner receives a request to record a transfer under section 49 of the Patent Act (section 104 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act promptly; once the application is open to public inspection or a transfer request is received, identity correction under this route may be foreclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for correcting applicant identity — PCT national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For a PCT national phase application, the request must be submitted before the earlier of: (a) the later of three months from national-phase entry and (if the Commissioner sent a subsection 154(7) notice before the end of those three months then) the day on which the three-month period after that notice expires; and (b) the day the Commissioner receives a request to record a transfer under section 49 (subsection 154(6) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCT national-phase timeline is more complex; track dates of national phase entry, any Commissioner notices under 154(7), and incoming transfer recording requests to determine applicable deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of applicant name (no identity change) — timing and statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An error that does not change identity (e.g., spelling/nickname) can be corrected by request from the applicant if submitted on or before payment of the final fee (or, if final fee refunded, on or before it is paid again). The request must include a statement that the correction does not add or delete an applicant or change identity (section 105 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the request includes the required statement; the timing cutoff is tied to final fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for requests to correct applicant naming/identity
rubrics_metrics.description: All correction requests must comply with requirements for written communications to the Commissioner. Every request must include application number, name of the applicant(s), a clear request indicating whether correction is for identity or name only, and any additional information required by sections 104, 105, or subsection 154(6) of the Patent Rules (see Section 2.02.01 in Chapter 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete requests may delay processing; include the prescribed statements and supporting materials as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of correction of an error in a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of an error in a patent application results in updating Office records; the requester will be informed by letter that the correction has been made if they requested notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections change Office records but are distinct from recording transfers or changes of name; follow notification preferences if you want confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting inventor naming errors — identity versus name and separate requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections to inventors follow similar identity vs name distinctions; requesters must state which type. If the inventor is also an applicant, a separate correction request for the applicant naming is required. Timelines for correcting inventor identities are generally longer than those for applicant identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Office will not adjudicate ownership disputes when processing inventorship corrections, parties should be prepared to pursue other legal remedies if ownership is contested.
